title: Blurring the Boundaries: Monsters in 'New Anthropology'
core_idea: The paper examines a Moscow Conceptualist's exploration of a 'new anthropology' through monstrous imagery in poetry and visual art, using interdisciplinary inter-art and comparative cultural critique to show how hybrid, androgynous figures challenge binaries (human/non-human, official/unofficial, normal/monstrous), reveal ideological mechanisms constructing deviance, and reconceptualize monsters as ontological mirrors that provoke a rethinking of boundaries shaping thought, culture, and power.
tldr: An interdisciplinary study of monstrous figures in Moscow Conceptualist art that uses hybridity and repetition to challenge binaries and ideological sameness, urging a rethink of human/monster boundaries.
